description: Three-panel composite of SEM fractographs of tensile-tested Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel, all secondary-electron fracture surfaces at the same magnification with a 20 µm scale bar printed in the bottom-right corner of each panel. (a) HR45: a rough, wavy ductile fracture surface showing large shallow depressions; an oval outline labelled "Dimples" encircles a cluster of equiaxed dimples in the centre-right, while two white arrows labelled "Microvoids" point to isolated small circular holes (upper left and lower centre). (b) HR68: a denser, more uniform dimple field with finer dimples; an oval labelled "Dimples" marks a fine-dimple region on the right, and three arrows labelled "Microvoids" mark deep holes on the left and lower-right. (c) HR82: a finer, more fibrous and equiaxed dimple morphology; an oval labelled "Dimples" marks a patch of small dimples in the upper-left, and three arrows labelled "Microvoids" mark larger voids at centre-right and along the bottom. In all three panels the surface is fully covered by tearing ridges and ductile dimples of varying size, consistent with a typical ductile transgranular fracture; no cleavage facets or intergranular facets are visible. The three panels together support the argument that increasing hot-rolling reduction from 45% to 82% refines the microstructure but preserves the dimpled ductile-fracture character, the HR45 surface carrying the coarsest dimples and HR68/HR82 finer, denser ones.
measured_quantities: dimple size (µm, assessed against the 20 µm scale bar, no numeric value printed)

observations.observation: All three panels are secondary-electron SEM images of tensile fracture surfaces with a 20 µm scale bar in the bottom-right corner of each, indicating comparable magnification across the group.
The fracture surfaces in (a) HR45, (b) HR68 and (c) HR82 are entirely covered by ductile dimples separated by tearing ridges; no cleavage or intergranular facets are visible.
Panel (a) HR45 shows the coarsest and largest dimples of the three panels, with wide shallow depressions.
Panels (b) HR68 and (c) HR82 show finer and more densely distributed dimples than (a), consistent with grain refinement with increasing rolling reduction.
Each panel carries two annotation types: an oval labelled "Dimples" enclosing a representative dimple cluster, and white arrows labelled "Microvoids" pointing to isolated holes.
Three microvoid arrows are shown in (b) and (c), whereas two are shown in (a).
The caption states that the fractographs correspond to the HR45, HR68 and HR82 samples respectively in panels (a), (b) and (c).
The citing text states that fractography of all hot-rolled samples shows a typical ductile fracture with a combination of ductile dimples and various microvoids.

The citing text attributes microvoid formation to debonding of intragranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles and to strain/stress concentration at intergranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles at austenite grain boundaries.
The citing text states that the dimple size in the HR45 sample was larger than in the HR68 and HR82 samples, attributed to its larger mean grain size.

The citing text states that with increasing rolling reduction the ductile fracture morphology was retained, suggesting toughness was barely affected, as also verified by Charpy impact test results in Fig. 5b.
No numeric dimple size, void fraction or other quantitative value is printed on any panel; only the 20 µm scale bar is given.

subfigures.description: SEM fractograph of the HR45 sample (20 µm scale bar). Coarse, wavy ductile fracture surface with large shallow dimples; an oval annotation labelled "Dimples" encircles an equiaxed dimple cluster, and two arrows labelled "Microvoids" indicate isolated small round holes.

SEM fractograph of the HR68 sample (20 µm scale bar). Denser, finer dimple field; oval annotation labelled "Dimples" on the right side and three arrows labelled "Microvoids" on the left/lower-right marking deeper holes.

SEM fractograph of the HR82 sample (20 µm scale bar). Fine, equiaxed/fibrous dimple morphology covering the surface; oval annotation labelled "Dimples" at upper-left and three arrows labelled "Microvoids" marking voids at centre-right and along the bottom.
